page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v6 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory. This yields an expansive memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture features modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), along with a large 260 MB L3 cache.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs and requiring attached network storage for persistent volumes. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core compute performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1975.0 and solid text processing throughput. Multi-core performance aligns with the 8-vCPU constraint, achieving 7972.24 in stress-ng and 7558.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory workloads, it supports 42.29 GB/sec read and 28.08 GB/sec write bandwidth on large blocks, with Redis SET throughput reaching 11.31 million operations per second.

Cost efficiency is centered around software licensing optimization. Constraining the 16-vCPU footprint down to 8 vCPUs preserves the full 128 GB memory allotment while reducing core-based software licensing expenses. Tradeoffs include lower composite memory scores in synthetic benchmarks and constrained multi-threaded execution ceilings, limiting utility for compute-bound scaling. The instance is suitable for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, and enterprise software that requires high RAM per core without high core licensing overhead.
